front.title: Pseudonymous Stapled Certificate Status Evidence for V2X and TLS with ITS Certificates (pOCSP)

author.organization: Telecom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris
Telecom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris
Telecom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris, and Institut CyberIA

abstract.t:
Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) systems authenticate broadcast and unicast messages with short-lived pseudonymous certificates. Revocation status validation is difficult in this environment: Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs) can be costly to distribute at pseudonym scale, while verifier-initiated OCSP requests introduce online dependencies, latency, metadata leakage, and denial-of-service exposure.
This document specifies pOCSP, an OCSP-derived response type and a set of deployment profiles for short-lived certificate-status evidence that is obtained by the certificate holder and stapled to an authenticated message or TLS CertificateEntry. A verifier validates pOCSP evidence locally, without contacting a responder at message- reception time. pOCSP retains the OCSP status semantics good, revoked, and unknown; defines an explicit signed usage context; defines a compact context-specific certificate identifier; and specifies deterministic, bounded validation, caching, and failure behavior. pOCSP does not claim that its identifier is unlinkable. The identifier is deterministic and can be correlated whenever the underlying certificate is observable or inferable. The V2X profiles therefore require single-certificate evidence and prohibit transmitting pOCSP evidence more frequently than the corresponding full certificate. The document prohibits future-active good evidence, bounds replay by mandatory thisUpdate and nextUpdate values, and makes an authenticated revocation terminal at the verifier: omitted, expired, unknown, or higher-versioned good evidence cannot mask it. It defines profiles for ETSI CAM/DENM, SAE J2735 messages, and TLS 1.3 with ITS certificates, requests an OCSP response-type object identifier, and establishes a registry of pOCSP profile identifiers.
